content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I have a question about [product_name] [version_no] transistor outputs: Is it possible to operate the outputs at high frequencies in the kHz range, for controlling devices such as stepper motor drives?
Short answer: no. You can check the specified limits in the [document].
No, this [product_name] is not the appropriate PLC for that application. The switching frequency of the transistor outputs is primarily constrained by the system cycle time.

Hi, Generally, relay outputs are much too slow for kHz-level switching; only transistor outputs can achieve such rates. Regarding [product_name] [version_no], you can review the technical specs in Appendix A of the [document] for basic and relay output modules. See details here: [url] Hope this clarifies things, [user_name]

[product_name] does not offer functionality for stepper motor control, especially if you're referring to pulse-and-direction type control. This product is designed as a 'smart relay', not a full PLC. You may want to try a more advanced PLC like [product_name] [version_no] or consider automation solutions from other well-known brands.

analysis.insight_summary: Users indicated that [product_name] [version_no] and its related hardware are not capable of providing the high-frequency transistor outputs necessary for stepper motor control. The technical constraints and lack of pulse-and-direction instructions mean it does not meet requirements for this use case.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] [version_no] and associated hardware to support high-frequency output switching suitable for stepper motor control, specifically at kHz range frequencies.
